commit.message: docs: add release notes entry for aux sig validation

lnwallet: require an aux sig per HTLC on taproot overlay channels

The aux signature blob is peer supplied and carries no count of its own.
Verification jobs were only built for HTLCs an entry was received for,
so a peer could withhold the aux signature for an HTLC simply by
omitting it: no job was produced, nothing reported the omission, and the
commitment became our state carrying a signature we never received. At
force close the resolver then reads an empty signature out of that
HTLC's custom records, and the second level HTLC cannot be swept.

An aux signer emits exactly one entry per non-dust HTLC, in lockstep
with the BTC level signatures, so the count is now checked the same way
those already are, right beside them.

The check is gated on the tapscript root bit rather than merely on an
aux signer being configured. The signer is attached node wide, so it is
also present on plain channels, whose peers correctly send no aux
signatures at all, and requiring them there would force close those
channels. That bit is set at funding time if and only if the negotiated
commitment type is a taproot overlay, so it names exactly the channels
whose peers owe us aux signatures.

lnwallet: model the aux sig blob faithfully in tests

Three places modelled the aux signature blob less faithfully than
production does, in ways that hid whether the blob was carried at all.

MockAuxSigner.UnpackSigs returned a single slot no matter how many HTLCs
were packed. A real aux signer emits exactly one slot per HTLC, and code
that pairs the unpacked slots with HTLCs by index depends on that. The
default mock now records the slot count in the packed blob and hands
back that many slots. Since the blob is parsed into custom records, it
has to stay a canonical TLV stream, so the count travels in the dummy
record's value. Registering a function rather than a fixed value is what
lets the result depend on the input.

restartChannel rebuilt the channel with no channel options, so a restart
silently dropped the aux signer and the restarted side stopped producing
aux signatures while its peer still expected them. Production re-applies
the aux components every time a channel is loaded.

Two chan sync tests rebuilt CommitSigs from a retransmitted wire message
without its aux signature blob, which the link carries across.

lnwallet: drop local session ref after combining partial sigs

MuSig2CombineSig removes the session from the signer's session manager once
all partial signatures have been combined, but MusigSession kept its
reference to the now-dead session. With the previous commit making the RBF
coop-close transitions release the session when a round ends, every
completed round then errored with 'session not found': Cleanup ran against a
session the signer had already dropped during the combine.

In this commit, we make CombineSigs use the haveAll return value it
previously discarded and clear its session reference once the final
signature has been produced, so the subsequent cleanup is a no-op. A new
regression test drives a full cooperative close round against the real
session manager and asserts that the post-round InvalidateNonce neither
errors nor leaks a session.

lnwallet+peer: release MuSig2 sessions on aborted coop-close rounds

A MusigChanCloser creates a fresh backing signer session every time
ProposalClosingOpts is called, overwriting the pointer to the previous one.
InvalidateNonce only dropped that pointer, so an RBF coop-close round that
never reached CombineSigs (peer disconnect after closing_complete, a fee
mismatch in the legacy flow, etc.) left one live session behind in the
signer's session manager for each aborted round.

In this commit, we make InvalidateNonce release the backing session via the
newly exported MusigSession.Cleanup, returning any cleanup error to the
caller. The chancloser MusigSession interface is updated accordingly, and
the RBF transitions now propagate the cleanup error. A regression test
drives five aborted rounds against a mock signer and asserts no session
survives each abort.
docs: add release note for invalid partial commit sig error

lnwallet: return InvalidPartialCommitSigError for bad partial sigs

VerifyCommitSig returns a *invalidPartialSigError when a MuSig2 partial
commitment signature fails to verify, but ReceiveNewCommitment matched
it with errors.As against a value target. The match never succeeded, so
the raw error was returned without the commitment height and
transaction.

Match against a pointer target instead, so the error is wrapped in an
InvalidPartialCommitSigError as intended.

Also add Unwrap to InvalidPartialCommitSigError, returning the embedded
InvalidCommitSigError. The link only sends the detailed error to the
remote peer when the error matches *InvalidCommitSigError, which an
InvalidPartialCommitSigError didn't do without Unwrap, so the peer would
still get the generic "invalid commitment" message.

docs: note MuSig2 session cleanup

In this commit, we add the v0.22.0 release note for the transient MuSig2 signer session cleanup.

lnwallet: release transient MuSig2 sessions

Taproot commitment signing and verification create stateful signer sessions. Once a partial signature has been sent to the peer or verified locally, the local signer no longer needs the backing session.

In this commit, we make the ownership split explicit. Commitment signatures sent to the peer use the signer cleanup flag, while verification releases its session after either success or failure. Initial channel funding and reestablish signing use the same transient path. Force-close and cooperative-close callers retain the existing behavior because they still combine the partial signatures locally.

The session tests now track the signer's live session set across repeated commitment rounds, invalid signatures, and the retained combine path.

commit.message:
docs: add release note for the offer store

Add the offer store to the BOLT 12 section of the 0.22.0 release notes.
The PR link holds a placeholder until the PR number is known.

offers: add offer store with insert and lookup

Introduce the offers package with a SQL-backed store for BOLT 12 offers.
The store keeps the encoded offer and the local state that the offer
string does not carry. It has an insert and a lookup by offer hash.
CreateOffer validates the parameters, encodes the offer and inserts it.
